# WHOI Research Facilities and Labs

> Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution's specialized research centers advancing marine science through radiocarbon dating, coral reef ecology, aquaculture innovation, and environmental systems research.

WHOI operates multiple state-of-the-art research facilities and laboratories focused on oceanographic research, marine ecology, and sustainable aquaculture. These facilities support cutting-edge investigations into climate change impacts on marine ecosystems, microbial ecology, and innovative farming practices.

## Key Topics

- Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI)
- Accelerator Mass Spectrometry (AMS)
- Radiocarbon Dating
- Coral Reef Research
- Aquaculture
- Marine Microbiology
- Climate Change
- Biogeochemistry
- Ocean Research
- Kelp Farming
- Shellfish Farming
- Environmental Systems
- Carbon Analysis
- Oceanographic Facilities

## Radiocarbon Dating & Biogeochemistry

- [NOSAMS](https://www2.whoi.edu/site/nosams/): National Ocean Sciences Accelerator Mass Spectrometry radiocarbon dating facility

## Marine Research Laboratories

- [Environmental Systems Laboratory](https://www2.whoi.edu/site/eslab/): WHOI marine research and aquaculture laboratory facility overview
- [Cohen Lab](https://www2.whoi.edu/site/cohenlab/): Research lab studying coral reefs, climate change, and marine ecosystems
- [Lindell Lab](https://www2.whoi.edu/site/lindell-lab/): Sustainable aquaculture research lab for kelp and shellfish farming

## Research Scientists

- [Amy Apprill](https://www2.whoi.edu/site/amy-apprill/): WHOI Associate Scientist profile: microbial ecology and coral reef research
